I gave the same prompt (a working diecast RX-7 with an animated Wankel engine, plus five reference photos) to Terra on Light and High, Sol on Medium, and Claude Opus 5.5 on Medium. Reference photos: Mazda RX-7 FD owned by @spicy.builds, photos by @dielowdrivers, via @dailyjdmcontent on Instagram. (The licence plate is blurred in the video.)
One test, one prompt: take it with a grain of salt and try it yourself.

articles.content:
I used Claude Opus 5.5 to build Tornado Redemption, a free tornado mod for Red Dead Redemption 2. Arthur, Micah, horses and wagons get swept up, with different tornado styles, a tornado gun and a jet powered balloon to play with.

Here's the finished mod, the funniest playtests, and how I built it with Claude Code: explain the idea, record myself testing it, give Claude the footage and feedback, then improve the next version. You can download the mod and its source below.

▼ Download the mod:
Latest release: https://github.com/mattvideoproductions/TornadoRedemption
Source code and instructions: https://github.com/mattvideoproductions/TornadoRedemption

INSTALL UPDATE: It's called NadoTest in the video, but the released version is Tornado Redemption. Copy TornadoRedemption.asi and TornadoRedemption.ini into your RDR2 game folder, alongside ScriptHookRDR2.dll AND dinput8.dll from Script Hook RDR2. Remove the old NadoTest.asi if upgrading so both versions don't load together.

Script Hook RDR2 by Alexander Blade: https://www.dev-c.com/rdr2/scripthookrdr2/
PC Story Mode only. Back up your saves; do not use it in Red Dead Online. Try the Low PC preset if performance struggles.

You're welcome to play with it, change it, fork it and share your own version under the included MIT license. I haven't uploaded it to Nexus Mods, but you're welcome to upload it there too—please retain the included license and copyright notice. I'm not promising ongoing updates, so feel free to take it further!

articles.content:
I gave Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Sol, and GPT-6 Luna the same creative briefs: a Blender animation about atoms, a Lemon vs Orange animation that turns into a playable boss fight, and an interactive CRT/VHS-style AI science special. Here are the actual results side by side, including what worked, what broke, and the little creative decisions that made one result feel more complete to me. These are three hands-on tests and my own reactions, not proof that one model wins every task. Opus impressed me most as a creative collaborator here; Sol and Luna are still capable agents at much lower standard API prices. The game test used Opus at high effort and Sol at extra-high, so keep that setting difference in mind. Which result would you actually want to watch or play?

articles.content:
GPT-6 Astra helped me build a playable jelly game in Unreal Engine. I also let it work on a separate 3D RPG without my playtesting—and those two projects changed how I think about getting useful results from AI. I show what the MattVidPro community is creating, walk through my jelly game's physics and garden, and explore the autonomous RPG's impressive details and rough edges.
